rationale: M59 (#825). Every line below is read off callsite-lines-825.c. c emitted NO line on any relationship before this pin (0 of 414 turn-audit sample), so the pre-fix state is 'unlined', and the two traps are the ways a line can be present and still wrong. (1) A newline-continued function-pointer member call: `call_expression` starts at the RECEIVER, so the construct-start line would stamp `run -> record` at 45 (`return c`) while the callee leaf `->record` is written on 46 — after the fix the line comes from the callee leaf. (2) A wrapped `struct` specifier: the specifier starts at the KEYWORD, so the construct-start line would put `Tally` at 15 and the wrapped use at 31, while the tag is written on 16 and 32. This second trap was NOT hypothetical — it was measured on jq jv_dtoa.c, where `struct` sits on 512 and `Bigint {` on 513, and the pre-fix analyzer put the reference edge on 512 (the audit's Tier-A check flagged it as the only inconsistency in 13,186 jq relationships). The forbidRelationships entries are exactly those pre-fix shapes, so re-introducing any of them fails the gate instead of passing silently. CONTRACT REPIN (2026-10-25): a QUOTED `#include` is the translation unit's own fragment (the preprocessor splices the header's text into this unit, so the file shares the unit's single scope) and is published as `part_of` with `partRole:"library"` and the part's MODULE SYMBOL as the target (the file stem); the path stays in `metadata.partPath`. An ANGLE include is another module's interface and keeps `imports`. This is a LABEL MOVE plus the target's space (path -> stem, because the arbiter resolves target strings against symbol names): no dependency is gained or lost, and each repinned row gains a forbid row pinning the same target in the old label so a revert goes red.

forbidRelationships.note: pre-fix shape: the call_expression (receiver) line; `->record` is written on 46

a QUOTED include is a part_of row now; the old imports label is forbidden so a revert goes red
